Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

AnophelesModel 2.0.0

Version 2 is a refactoring of AnophelesModel version 1 (last release v1.1.0), developed as AnophelesModel2. It keeps the entomological model of the mosquito feeding cycle (Chitnis et al.) and the host / activity databases, but the intervention framework and API were rewritten and are not backward compatible.

Host-seeking killing names

  • Host-seeking killing is named KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute (efficacy component) and killing_during_host_seeking_absolute (batch column), formerly HostSeekingKilling / host_seeking_killing, so that it is clear it is the absolute rate (consistent with AnophelesEntoTrials). The relative value of the hut trial fits is KillingDuringHostSeekingRelative in ITN_parameterisations_Champagne2025 (formerly KillingDuringHostSeeking); get_ITN_params(rescale_hsk = FALSE) returns it under that name. Former and relative names give an error naming the absolute one (a former batch column would otherwise have run the standard model). The decay suffix _hsk (halflife_hsk, OpenMalaria placeholders) is unchanged.

Correctness and input validation

  • Explicit per-component insecticide decay shapes always take priority over linear half-lives. Constant shapes need no decay parameters; incomplete non-constant specifications and zero or NaN linear half-lives now raise errors identifying the component and parameter-set row.
  • Intervention interfaces reject unnamed, duplicate, missing or invalid efficacies, out-of-range coverages (including uncertainty draws), and non-positive or non-finite durations. Positive subday durations use one time point consistently. Host-seeking killing remains a non-negative rate that can exceed one; optional batch NA values still mean inactive.
  • def_host_params() orders custom host tables as human then animal, so reversing input rows no longer changes host parameters or model results. The species_name column of custom host tables is optional (host parameters are species-independent).
  • Incubation-survival sums now include the term at index zero when it is their only term. This corrects custom parameterisations with longer resting durations or shorter incubation periods; bundled parameterisations retain their existing results.
  • calculate_combined_impact() handles complete deterrency and killing without dividing by zero when no mosquitoes reach a feeding stage.
  • Impact calculations now raise an error for a zero baseline vectorial capacity (relative reduction is undefined) or non-finite results, instead of silently reporting zero impact. The message names the time point and the parameter sets concerned (and the draw in run_interventions(), or the intervention in calculate_impact()).
  • get_ITN_params(mode = "dummy_host"): the insecticide decay of the rescaled host-seeking killing uses the trial’s own aging time (new aged_time column of ITN_parameterisations_Champagne2025: 3 years, 2 for Sovegnon); it was always 3 years, so Sovegnon’s host-seeking killing decayed 1.5 times too slowly. get_ITN_params() also documents mode in its result.
  • calculate_combined_impact() rebuilds both interventions’ daily effects from their parameters ($param_set, duration, insecticide_decay) with the supplied model_p, as calculate_impact(): results no longer depend on the model used to build the interventions. It accepts overlaps exactly at their bounds (e.g. coverages 0.8 and 0.8 with overlap 0.6), which floating-point arithmetic rejected.
  • One-day (and shorter) batches with several parameter sets: the attrition matrix keeps one row per parameter set (it was transposed, giving an error).
  • More inputs that were silently accepted are errors (fail loudly): component_decay elements without decay or with unknown fields; L_* / kappa_* batch columns without decay_*; a missing decay_attrition column, and attrition columns are matched exactly (the old L / kappa / decay column names, and $ partial matching, could pick up another column); vector values of single arguments of build_intervention(); an invalid insecticide_decay; uncertainty draws mixing the standard and dummy-host models; custom vector tables without the model’s columns (M, Chi, A0, zeta.3, td, tau, ts; a missing tau became 1 day) or out of range; an extrinsic incubation period shorter than the resting duration (was raised to it), or not a whole number of days (the survival sums need whole days, and the OpenMalaria export rounded it); unknown activity pattern IDs. Attrition errors name the parameter-set row; the Weibull fit warns when it stops at the iteration limit.
  • Misspelled component names in halflife_insecticide / component_decay (e.g. Preprandial), and misspelled decay columns of run_interventions() batch tables (e.g. halflife_pree), are errors: they were silently ignored, leaving the effect without its decay.
  • Activity patterns combined with c() (instead of list(), one per taxon) are an error in get_OM_ento_snippet() and calculate_exposure(): their duplicated entries silently gave every taxon the first pattern.

Vector bionomics from AnophelesBionomics

  • vec_ent_param now comes from AnophelesBionomics (posterior means and sds of its hierarchical Bayesian model), replacing the older parameterisation. Results differ from version 1.
  • Taxa have an explicit level (species, complex, genus), a parent complex and imputed_traits (parameters without data of their own). def_vector_params() gains level; list_all_species() returns a data frame of taxa.
  • An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii are merged as "Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii", the new default species; the old names are accepted with a warning. Complexes are named by their label (e.g. "Gambiae").
  • tau (resting duration) is estimated per taxon from the fed / gravid ratio (1.07 days for An. gambiae ss/coluzzii, about 2 days for the genus) instead of the fixed value 3. In the survival over the extrinsic incubation period it is rounded to whole days (at least one); the former silent replacement of tau < 2 by 2 is removed.
  • Chi is the indoor human blood index by default; indoor and outdoor HBI are both stored and def_vector_params(hbi = "outdoor" | "weighted") selects another one.
  • read_bionomics_table() and def_vector_params(bionomics_table = ) use a newer bionomics table without reinstalling. The dataset is regenerated with the scripts in data-raw/.

Export to OpenMalaria

  • New demo of the export: demo("OM_export", package = "AnophelesModel") (mosquito populations with species-specific activity patterns, ITNs, XML text, scenario values; its last part needs openMalariaUtilities).
  • get_OM_ento_snippet() is rewritten: it returns the input lists of openMalariaUtilities::defineEntomology() (no XML nodes; the XML dependency is removed). It fixes the mapping of the original version, which wrote the resting duration tau as mosqSeekingDuration and hardcoded mosqRestDuration = 2: now mosqRestDuration = tau in whole days and mosqSeekingDuration = td. With activity patterns, each species is split into _indoor1 / _indoor2 / _outdoor populations by human exposure, with indoor / outdoor human blood indices.
  • New get_OM_GVI_snippet(): generic vector intervention for openMalariaUtilities::defineVectorControl(), one component per effect with its own decay (exact when possible, fitted Weibull for attrition x insecticide decay), acting on populations exposed in bed (ITN) or resting indoors (IRS). For dummy-host interventions it has deterrency and post-prandial killing only (no pre-prandial killing).
  • New define_OM_vector_control() / deploy_OM_vector_control(): write a whole ITN / IRS intervention into an openMalariaUtilities baseList, with one <deployment> holding all its components (same people) and one deploy per campaign of a schedule (dates, numeric or placeholder coverages). The define writes the components, the deploy the deployment (the schedule is given only there). Defines and deploys can come in any order: components are always written before the deployments, as OpenMalaria requires (also with add_OM_GVI()). Host-seeking killing of dummy-host nets is exported as the model’s dummy host: per campaign, an OpenMalaria added non-human host (addNonHumanHosts, availability relative to an adult human = coverage × KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute / human availability, biting probability 0) whose availability decays as the GVI effects do: attrition × insecticide decay of host-seeking killing, exact when it is a single OpenMalaria decay, otherwise the Weibull fitted to the product (one nonHumanHostsModifications per host, <name>_dummy_<k>_decay, with an increasing decay; placeholders @<name>_hsk_L@ / _k@ like the other effects). Written by the deploy (once, with the whole schedule); it needs OpenMalaria schema >= 46 (checked with 49), from the baseList’s OMVersion. OpenMalaria scales an added host by the availability of an average adult (the hut sleeper), so relative to the average human the host-seeking killing is stronger than in the package’s model (by the adult / mean availability ratio, 1.35 in the scenario checked); this choice may be revisited. A named list of interventions defines one intervention whose values are chosen per scenario, e.g. to loop scenarios over net types.
  • Age-restricted deployments need both minAge and maxAge (or neither, all ages); a single limit, negative ages or minAge >= maxAge are errors.
  • Checked in OpenMalaria, through openMalariaUtilities, on the entomological outputs: standard ITNs deployed by campaigns (OpenMalaria 44 and 49); dummy-host nets, a named list of nets with placeholder decays, IRS (both irs_exposure definitions), age-restricted, cumulative and continuous deployments (OpenMalaria 49). For dummy-host nets, timing, coverage, replacement by later campaigns, populations reached and lifespan are as designed, and the decay of the added hosts follows the written decay within 0.3% of the initial effect. The plain-text route writes the same XML as the openMalariaUtilities route. Not run in OpenMalaria: sub-population deployments (subpop).
  • om_scenario_values(): decay columns with fixed decays are an error even when nothing else needs filling; attrition columns on a net without attrition, and a kappa column on a shape-less attrition, are errors (they had no effect); factor columns are read as values; an undeployed dummy-host intervention is always an error.
  • get_OM_GVI_snippet() warns that host-seeking killing of dummy-host interventions is not in the GVI (nor written by add_OM_GVI()).
  • Without the indoor/outdoor split (get_OM_ento_snippet() without activity), the GVI export warns that the intervention acts on all the bites, outdoor ones included (get_OM_GVI_snippet(), define_OM_vector_control(), get_OM_xml()).
  • Populations with a share of 0 (e.g. indoor2 when the in-bed and IRS shares are equal, or a species with a species_shares of 0) are not written (their annualEIR would be 0); om_ento_values() warns when a composition gives a species a share of 0.
  • Placeholder names that would collide are errors: two populations, or two interventions of a baseList, whose names give the same cleaned placeholder (e.g. "IG 2" and "IG_2").
  • All schedule dates (om_campaigns(), schedules, end_date, om_continuous()) must be "YYYY-MM-DD" (or Date objects); formats such as "2021/01/01" were accepted by campaigns only.
  • The Weibull fitted to attrition × insecticide decay (fitted_decay, used by the OpenMalaria export) no longer has an amplitude: it starts at 1, as the curve written to OpenMalaria, so the fit is the curve that is used (an amplitude was fitted, then ignored). fitted_decay has columns component, L, kappa, rmse.
  • The warnings on unusual attrition (IRS with attrition, ITN without) are given on every export route (also define_OM_vector_control() / get_OM_xml() with placeholder decays or a list of nets), not only for a single net with fixed decays.
  • The OpenMalaria export writes the L of decays ending at L (step, linear, smooth-compact) rounded towards zero, with 10 digits: rounding up kept the protection beyond its end (a 45-day step ended after day 45).
  • IRS can reach the mosquitoes resting indoors (endophily, default) or those biting indoors: get_OM_ento_snippet(irs_exposure = "indoor_resting" | "indoor_biting") sets the population split of the OpenMalaria export accordingly; in the vectorial capacity calculation, the same choice is the exposure passed (indoor_resting or Exposure_Indoor_total). Documented in the vignette.
  • Dummy hosts in OpenMalaria: each campaign replaces the nets of its recipients, as the GVI does (a component redeployed to a person is refreshed, not stacked): earlier dummy hosts are reduced by the coverage of every later campaign (<name>_dummy_<j>_replaced_<k>, constant availability reduction = the campaign’s coverage or its placeholder). Before, cohorts accumulated (two campaigns at 100% gave twice the host-seeking killing while the GVI stayed at one net).
  • om_scenario_values(): half-life and shape columns are independent overrides (a kappa column alone changes the shape and keeps the half-life); with combine = FALSE, the net’s own decay parameters are kept for what is not supplied. Values are validated (positive, shape where needed), errors naming rows and effect.
  • define_OM_entomology() writes the animal host parameters of om_ento (hosts_p) instead of openMalariaUtilities’ fixed values, so both routes write the same entomology.
  • New om_continuous(): continuous deployment at target ages (e.g. EPI, school), with coverage and optional begin / end, accepted as schedule by deploy_OM_vector_control() and get_OM_xml() (standard model; same structure as openMalariaUtilities’ deploy_cont_compat()).
  • Schema version: 44 by default; get_OM_xml(schema = ) or the baseList’s OMVersion. From 49, the entomology has no propInfected / propInfectious (removed in 49; also dropped by define_OM_entomology()). Standard interventions are the same in 44 and 49.
  • Placeholders only where something varies: efficacies with several nets, decays with define_OM_vector_control(decay = "placeholder") (otherwise written from the nets), dummy-host availabilities unless the net and the coverages are fixed.
  • New om_scenario_values(): fills these placeholders in the user’s own scenario table, row by row (net from a column, coverages from the columns named like the schedule’s placeholders), from the baseList or the get_OM_xml() result, which keep what was written. Decays: by default one attrition column (years, or decay_unit = "days") combined with each effect’s insecticide decay (the dummy hosts take the attrition as it is); combine = FALSE for final decays per effect. Computed once per distinct net and decay.
  • New om_vector_control(): specifies an intervention for the OpenMalaria export from its efficacies (or a get_ITN_params() parameterisation) and decays, without a model or a duration; the export builds it with the entomology of the scenario and fits Weibull decays over 3 years (ITN) or 1 year (IRS) by default (fit_years). Intervention objects of build_intervention() remain accepted.
  • New om_campaigns(): campaign schedules from regular dates (from, to, every, as seq.Date()) or given dates, with one coverage (number or placeholder), one per campaign, or one placeholder per year (by_year = TRUE, as byyear of deploy_it_compat()), and optionally the end_date of the period (life of the dummy hosts), kept with the schedule so that deploy and get_OM_xml() need no end_date argument.
  • In a list of interventions (template), each effect keeps its decay function when all the interventions share it (e.g. a step for historical nets), with its parameters as placeholders; it is a Weibull only when the decay functions differ.
  • New define_OM_entomology(): writes the entomology with defineEntomology() (seasonality as numbers or placeholders, by default @m1@…@m12@, which need a recent openMalariaUtilities; scaledAnnualEIR) and keeps it in the baseList; define_OM_vector_control() takes the mosquito populations and parameters from there (no om_ento argument), so the interventions are consistent with the entomology.
  • get_OM_ento_snippet() also returns muvA (in shares) and the model of each mosquito population (model_params, whose human availability scales the dummy hosts).
  • The OpenMalaria export follows the model’s priorities for insecticide decay: an explicit shape, then a linear half-life (NA: unspecified).
  • Relative contribution of the species to the EIR: each population’s annualEIR is its relative contribution (species share × share within the species), the total EIR being set with scaledAnnualEIR on <entomology>. eir_shares() computes species shares from relative abundances and sporozoite rates; get_OM_ento_snippet(species_shares = ) writes the contributions as numbers, and without it as placeholders @contrib_<population>@, filled by om_ento_values() for one or several species compositions. Shares that do not sum to 1, or do not match the taxa, are errors.
  • New get_OM_xml(): the entomology and vector control as XML text, without openMalariaUtilities, to paste into an existing scenario: one snippet for the entomology (<vector>, same structure as defineEntomology() but with the animal host parameters of hosts_p), and per intervention one for the components (define), one for the deployment (deploy) and, for dummy-host interventions, the dummy hosts and their decays. It shares the list builders of define_OM_vector_control() / deploy_OM_vector_control(), so both routes write the same XML.
  • New add_OM_GVI(): writes these interventions into an openMalariaUtilities baseList, as a single component when the three decays are identical and one component per effect otherwise (openMalariaUtilities in Suggests).
  • build_intervention() keeps its inputs in $settings (used by the export).

New

  • build_intervention() builds an intervention from user-supplied efficacies (Deterrency, PrePrandial, PostPrandial, KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute), an attrition decay and optional per-component insecticide decay.
  • run_interventions() evaluates many parameter sets × coverages in one vectorised call, with zipped uncertainty draws (vec_param_sets, interv_param_sets, exposure_sets, coverage_sets).
  • get_ITN_params() / list_ITN_params() load ITN efficacies and insecticide decay fitted to experimental hut trials (ITN_parameterisations_Champagne2025). The dataset has a fit column: a trial fitted in several parts (Sovegnon) has one control per fit, and host-seeking killing is rescaled by the control of the net’s own fit.
  • Dummy-host model: host-seeking killing (KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute) adds a fourth host type whose availability is the absolute killing rate (in the units of the host availabilities, not a probability). It is mutually exclusive with pre-prandial killing. get_ITN_params(mode = "dummy_host") converts the hut-trial estimates, which are relative to the control-arm availability alpha_0, to absolute values by multiplying by alpha_0 of the same arm (rescale_hsk = FALSE returns the relative value). The hut model’s rates are per hut-night while the package uses per-day rates; by provisional convention a hut-night is treated as a day (no conversion by the host-seeking duration td), pending an improved experimental hut fitting model.
  • Insecticide decay: per-component linear decay (halflife_insecticide, years, a time-to-zero calibrated so that efficacy at the washed arm’s aging time, 3 years or 2 for Sovegnon, equals the 20x-washed value) or any decay shape (component_decay). The insecticide_decay = FALSE switch keeps unwashed efficacies throughout. With TRUE, build_intervention() also returns fitted_decay, one Weibull per component approximating attrition × insecticide decay.
  • decay_function() supports weibull, exponential, hill, linear, step, smooth-compact and none/constant, following OpenMalaria conventions (L is a half-life for weibull/exponential/hill and a time to zero for linear/step/smooth-compact); values always stay in [0, 1].
  • calculate_combined_impact() supports dummy-host interventions (host-seeking killing is additive for people covered by both products).

Changed

  • build_model_obj(vec_p, hosts_p) no longer takes activity patterns or total_pop; Nv0 is no longer an argument anywhere. Host populations are unit-sized and vectorial capacity reduction is scale-invariant.
  • Exposure acts on coverage, not on efficacies. Version 1 adjusted the intervention effects by indoor/in-bed exposure (adjustment_for_location). Now calculate_exposure() (formerly get_in_out_exp(), same calculation) gives an exposure factor passed as exposure to calculate_impact() / run_interventions(), which use the effective coverage coverage × exposure.
  • calculate_impact() always computes impact relative to coverage 0, even if coverage_vec does not start with 0 (previously relative to its first element). calculate_impact(), run_interventions() and calculate_combined_impact() share one vectorised engine.
  • calculate_impact() is run_interventions() applied to the parameters stored in each intervention ($param_set, added by build_intervention()) and returns the same data.table (one row per intervention and coverage, with intervention, name, the parameters, coverage, exposure, avg_vc, avg_impact) instead of the nested list of version 1. The model parameters all come from model_p. Interventions are combined with c(); objects not made by build_intervention() are rejected.
  • keep_time = TRUE in calculate_impact() and run_interventions() also returns the vectorial capacity and impact on each day, for all parameter sets.
  • plot_impact() replaces plot_impact_species() and plot_impact_var(): it plots the output of both functions, with the median and 95% interval when there are uncertainty draws. ggpubr and Hmisc are no longer suggested.
  • calculate_combined_impact() evaluates both interventions over the shorter duration (one point per day) and reports the assigned coverages via message().

Removed

  • Intervention database and its functions: def_interventions_effects(), get_net_types(), get_net_insecticides(), get_net_decay(), list_available_interventions(), list_intervention_models(), and the datasets interventions_param and intervention_obj_examples. Use build_intervention() / get_ITN_params() instead.
  • AnophelesModel(), calculate_impact_var(), calculate_impact_ip(), calculate_combined_impact_var(); use run_interventions() for variability and uncertainty.
  • get_exposure_multiplier() (exposure now acts on coverage, see above).
  • The XML-node outputs of get_OM_ento_snippet() / get_OM_GVI_snippet() (see “Export to OpenMalaria” above for their replacements).
